t:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act—

    (1) 
not less than $2,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for Science Education Support shall be available for the “Student Science Training” program;
 
    (2) 
not less than $4,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for Science Education Support shall be available for the “Undergraduate Research Participation” program;
 
    (3) 
not to exceed $59,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for National and Special Research Programs shall be available for the “Research Applied to National Needs” program.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "Participation" signals outside involvement, but it appears only in the proper name of a funded program. The section merely sets minimum and maximum amounts of appropriated funds for particular science programs. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision.
fable.s: not less than $4,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for Science Education Support shall be available for the “Undergraduate Research Participation” program

qwen_block.w: This section merely allocates specific funding amounts to various programs. The term 'Participation' appears only as part of the proper name of a grant/program ('Undergraduate Research Participation'), not as a description of a process where outside parties consult with the government on a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants and warns against matching keywords in proper nouns.
qwen_block.s: not less than $4,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for Science Education Support shall be available for the “Undergraduate Research Participation” program;
qwen_block.b:
Temptation: The word "Participation" appears in the name of the "Undergraduate Research Participation" program, which might suggest that students are participating in a decision-making process.
Resolution: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits, grants, or programs are not participation. Furthermore, the mere appearance of the word "participation" in a proper noun or program title without an actual outside-party process (like a hearing or advisory board) is a trap. This section only allocates funding amounts.

opus.w: This section only sets aside funds for named programs. The word "Participation" appears only in the program's proper name, which the definition rules out as a trap. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities or right to sue is created, so no outside party takes part in a federal decision.
opus.s: not less than $4,000,000 of the sum stipulated in section 1 for Science Education Support shall be available for the “Undergraduate Research Participation” program
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section names an "Undergraduate Research Participation" program. That fails the definition: the word appears only in a program's proper name. The section just sets aside money for three programs and gives no process for consulting or coordinating with outside parties before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section allocates funds to specific programs, including one named 'Undergraduate Research Participation.' However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, or programs from the definition of participation. The term 'participation' here refers to students engaging in research activities, not to outside parties consulting with the government on a federal decision. Therefore, this is a funding allocation, not a participation requirement.
